item.title: Ex-Pakistan PM Khan taken back to jail after hospital checks
item.description: Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was transferred back to jail early on Friday, hours after being taken to a hospital for court-ordered medical checks, the government said. The Supreme Court ordered on Tuesday that Khan, Pakistan's most popular politician, be taken to the private Shifa International Hospital in the capital Islamabad within 48 hours for treatment, after his lawyers petitioned the court over concerns that his health was poor. The ex-cricket captain and his wife Bushra Bibi, who is also his spiritual guide, were both sentenced late last year to 17 years in prison. Publicado también por: The Hindu - International, BBC News - World, Al Jazeera English. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: What a record-breaking El Nino could mean for the world
item.description: This year's El Nino is on track to be the strongest on record, threatening to unleash extreme weather across the globe and make 2027 the hottest recorded year by far. It is expected to be the most "intense" El Nino in more than a century, the head of long-range forecasting at the UK's Met Office warned on Friday. Stacked on top of long-term human-caused climate change, the temporary jolt will offer a glimpse of the heat the world can expect by the late 2030s, experts say. Publicado también por: Phys.org. Fuente: France 24 - English.

Sin embargo, la brecha con los hombres sigue siendo grande. Detrás de esta diferencia hay factores que van mucho más allá de las decisiones individuales: menores ingresos, trayectorias laborales más interrumpidas por tareas de cuidado, menos acceso histórico al sistema financiero y una cultura que durante décadas mantuvo a las mujeres alejadas de las finanzas. En este episodio de #DWCómoteAfecta analizamos por qué las mujeres siguen invirtiendo menos que los hombres, qué obstáculos enfrentan y qué cambios podrían ayudar a cerrar esta brecha. | DW Español
